evidence.quote: AMT-061 (AAV5-hFIXco-Padua; etranacogene dezaparvovec)

The IMP is identified as AAV5-hFIXco-Padua (hereafter referred as AMT-061; etranacogene dezaparvovec). AMT-061 is a recombinant adeno-associated viral vector of serotype 5 (AAV5) containing the Padua variant of a codon-optimized human factor IX cDNA under the control of a liver-specific promoter.
The pharmaceutical form of AMT-061 is a solution for IV infusion.
Subjects will receive a single IV infusion of 2 x 1013 gc/kg AMT-061.
Since this is a gene therapy trial in which the IMP is administered to human subjects as a one-time only dose

The AMT-060 and AMT-061 based gene therapy vectors are identical with the exception of a two-nucleotide substitution resulting in a single codon change (AGG to CTG) in the coding sequence for factor IX, corresponding to an Arginine to Leucine substitution in the transgenic protein.
The R338L substitution, FIX-Padua, represents a naturally occurring variant of factor IX
Both AMT-060 and AMT-061 employ the same AAV5 capsid as vector and liver-specific promoter, conferring similar safety and expression profiles.

notes: Document: CT-AMT-061-01 Version 4.0 (Amendment 3.0), 08 Feb 2022. Printed page numbers equal the PDF page numbers (pages 1-112; PDF page 113 is an electronic signature page). Redactions: the posted PDF is redacted (CCI/PPD); patient-reported-outcome and some questionnaire names are blank in the text layer (rows 'CCI' in soa_activities), lab names in Appendix 13.1 are redacted (PPD), and the content after Section 5.1 on page 54 (Table 6 'Components of AMT-061 Drug Product', listed in the List of In-Text Tables, and Section 5.2) is blank in the text layer, so manufacturing_or_source is null. Two blank slots in the abbreviation list (between BDD-FVIII and cDNA, and between EU and FDA, page 10) are likely redacted entries and could not be read. product: only AMT-061 is an investigational product; no lymphodepleting product. Not recorded as products: AMT-060 (predecessor product, background only), the short-acting factor IX challenge dose (40 IU/kg) used for the factor IX recovery assessment, and prednisolone for transaminase elevation (Table 7). The product type is recorded as 'gene therapy' (page 52 wording); the protocol does not print a type label such as 'AAV gene therapy'. immunogenicity: specimen is not stated for anti-AAV5 total/neutralizing antibodies, anti-factor IX antibodies or factor IX inhibitors (only 'Blood & semen sampling' in the SoA); units/titer units are not stated for any assay in this trial (titers 1/340 and 1/1000 on page 40 refer to AMT-060 and NHP data). Method is not stated for anti-factor IX antibodies or capsid-specific T cells (ELISpot appears only in the AMT-060 background, page 35). Timing for central factor IX inhibitors: Section 6.1.3 says Week 6, 12, 26 and 52; Table 2 also marks Screening and D0 pre IMP. Footnote d/f says re-test 'with two weeks'; Section 6.2.3.6 says 'preferably within two weeks'. Appendix 13.1 lists 'IgG antibodies AAV5/IgM antibodies AAV5' and 'Neutralizing antibodies to AAV5' under different referral-testing blocks (lab names redacted). Conflicts: (1) Hematology: Table 8 (page 74) includes 'CD4+ count' in Hematology, the SoA footnote i (pages 23, 26) does not; the SoA has a separate screening-only row 'HIV, viral load, CD4+' and Appendix 13.1 lists 'CD4 counts' separately; both hematology versions recorded. (2) Serology: Table 8 says 'HIV viral load'; SoA row says 'HIV, viral load, CD4+'; exclusion criterion refers to an HIV serological test; Appendix 13.1 adds 'HIV-1/2 Antibody differentiation test' as confirmation testing. (3) ALT is 'alanine aminotransferase' in the abbreviation list and Table 2/4/8 legends but 'alanine transaminase (ALT)' in Table 4 footnote j (page 26); AST is 'aspartate aminotransaminase (AST)' in the synopsis (page 15). (4) Table 8 legend has 'HCB: hepatitis C virus' (typo for HCV) and 'HbeAg'. (5) Factor IX protein concentration: Section 6.2.2.3 says central and/or local laboratory as indicated in Table 2, while Table 2 lists it under Central Laboratory only. (6) Table 8 lists the central chemistry analytes with 'gamma-glutamyltransferase' while the SoA footnotes add '(ɣGT)'; Table 8 analytes are recorded. Serum chemistry at D0 post IMP is CRP only (Table 2; Section 6.1.2.2: CRP at 3 hours). Cross-references: both targets (Table 2, Table 4) are the SoA laboratory flow charts themselves; found on pages 21-23 and 25-26. genetic_testing: only factor IX gene sequencing. Vector integration analysis (nr LAM PCR, page 41) is preclinical background, not a trial assessment; replication-competent virus appears only as an example in AE special-notification criteria (page 78); no HLA typing; APOE in the abbreviation list refers to the AMT-060 background promoter construct. endpoint_assays: no PK, cellular kinetics or biodistribution assay in this trial; units are stated only for factor IX activity (% of normal units) and factor IX recovery (IU/ml per U/kg); vector genome detection has no units. Liver Sample for Future Research recorded as 'other' (optional consent, Amendment 3.0). panels: specimen is stated only for serum chemistry (panel name 'Serum Chemistry', 'Serum electrolytes') and inflammatory markers ('Blood samples'). Abbreviations not in the list but used: CD4+/CD4, PBMC, PT (defined in body page 29 as prothrombin time), CSR (defined page 15), PROs (page 14), e-diary (page 59), AESI (page 105); 'hr' in '24-hr stay at clinic' (the list has 'h' = hour).
